- R-001: App makes zero network calls and includes no third-party SDKs (including analytics/crash reporting); SwiftData ModelContainer is audited for cloudKitDatabase: .none.
- R-002: Native stack only: SwiftUI, SwiftData, Core Image/Metal, Swift Charts, StoreKit 2, targeting iOS 17+.
- R-003: Daily check-in (mood pick, 1-2 chip taps) completes with a haptic+spring reveal ceremony; cold launch to revealed card takes under 10 seconds of active interaction with zero forced tutorial.
- R-004: Check-in is non-committing until its final step: a force-quit mid-flow restarts cleanly on relaunch with no daily-lock consequence.
- R-005: Daily lock is keyed to the last-completed calendar day in the timezone active at completion; verified by changing the Simulator's date/timezone forward, backward, and across a DST boundary without producing a duplicate or skipped day.
- R-006: International date-line/transoceanic travel may legitimately produce a same-trip double check-in or an apparent one-day streak gap — documented as an accepted limitation, not treated as a bug.
- R-007: Generative engine is deterministic: identical (date + mood + chips [+ frozen time-of-day]) inputs on the same simulated day always render byte-identical output.
- R-008: Different day/mood/chip combinations render meaningfully different compositions (palette, shape-field topology, particle/line density); verified by generating and visually inspecting 8-10+ combinations side by side, not just confirming they render.
- R-009: Generative output reads as genuinely beautiful abstract art (painterly gradient blooms / particle fields / flow-field lines), not a literal illustration or a gradient-picker demo; Simulator-only visual review is explicitly noted as not equivalent to on-device review.
- R-010: Caption engine selects deterministically from a curated local phrase bank with a 30-day no-repeat window per mood.
- R-011: Aura+ regeneration uses an added seed nonce layered on the base seed and must differ from the original in at least 2 of {palette, shape-field topology, particle/line density} for identical date/mood/chip inputs.
- R-012: Regeneration credit and the daily lock share one canonical 'last completed calendar day' state; free tier gets 0 regenerations/day, Aura+ gets 1/day; rolling the device clock cannot grant extra regenerations.
- R-013: A mid-day Aura+ purchase never retroactively mutates an already-persisted card's render; entitlement state is snapshotted at generation time.
- R-014: Each card is rendered once and persisted via SwiftData as an image+recipe record; widget, archive, and export all read this cached render and never re-invoke the generative engine live.
- R-015: A SwiftData store load failure (corruption, disk full, migration failure) is detected and surfaced as an explicit, distinguishable error state, never silently presented as a fresh empty store.

Re-emit a SINGLE corrected ```tasks-json``` fenced block — the whole backlog, not a diff — that adds or updates tasks (via requirement_ids) so every one of these is covered by at least one task.
MACHINE CONTRACT (required): in your wrap-up, alongside the prose, emit ONE fenced ```tasks-json``` block containing a single JSON object of the form {"tasks": [{"id": "T-001", "title": ..., "owner_lane": ..., "files": [...], "depends_on": [], "acceptance_criteria": [...], "requirement_ids": ["R-001"], "status": "pending"}]}. owner_lane must be one of: data_domain, primary_ui, services_utilities, polish_resilience. depends_on lists task ids and the graph must be acyclic. requirement_ids lists the id(s) from requirements.json this task fulfills — every CORE requirement needs at least one task naming it, or the build is missing part of what was promised. The build workers are assigned their lane's tasks from this block, so make it complete.
